newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, Czechs consider US$65 mln plane venture.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, Czechs consider US$65 mln plane venture.

text.p: Taiwan is considering setting up a US$65 million venture with Aero Vodochody of the Czech Republic to jointly develop and produce nine-seat aircraft, the cabinet's aviation committee said on Friday.

"After a year's negotiation, we expect Han Hsiang Aerospace Industry Co to sign the US$65 million deal with Aero Vodochody by the end of this year," an official at the Committee for Aviation and Space Industry Development said by telephone.
"But I must say although both sides have discussed details, a final agreement has yet to be made," he said.
He said each side would hold half of the venture, which would produce Ae270 turboprops.
"According to an initial agreement, Aero Vodochody and Han Hsiang each will produce part of the plane's key components and parts, and then have them assembled in Taiwan," he said.
"We estimate the deal to have sales potential of 1,000 turboprops in future production. With each priced at US$1.3 million, that will turn out total sales of US$1.3 billion."
Sales would focus on Eastern Europe and Russia but the proposed venture also has East Asian ambitions. "We also hope to develop the mainland China market," the official said.

Han Hsiang Aerospace Industry Co resulted from parliament's May 1995 conversion of Taiwan's military aircraft production centre, Aero Industry Development Centre, into a state company making civilian planes and parts.
Han Hsiang is supervised by the economics ministry. Before the conversion, it was under the defence ministry.
